name: VerSe 2020: Large Scale Vertebrae Segmentation Challenge
description: VerSe 2020 (Large Scale Vertebrae Segmentation Challenge 2020) was organized in conjunction with MICCAI 2020 to advance automated spine analysis in computed tomography (CT). The benchmark consists of multi-detector spine CT examinations from 300 subjects (yielding 303 series and over 4,000 individually visualized vertebrae) acquired across multi-center clinical workflows from all four major CT manufacturers (GE, Philips, Siemens, Canon). VerSe 2020 specifically evaluates algorithm robustness in the presence of challenging anatomical anomalies (including transitional vertebrae like lumbarized L6 or thoracicized T13, enumerative variations, osteophytes, and surgical fixation hardware). Annotations include voxel-level semantic segmentation masks and 3D anatomical centroid coordinates for every individual cervical (C1–C7), thoracic (T1–T12), and lumbar (L1–L5/L6) vertebra.
